# Hypotheses and verdicts

*Generated by `task report` from `results/`; do not edit by hand.*

Decision rules live in `config/hypotheses.yaml`; verdicts are computed from `results/` by `kapitalkompass.mlops.hypotheses`.

- **Pre-registered (H1–H4):** the hypothesis file, the drift design and the held-out questions were committed (commit `96a0303`, Day 7) before the experiments that test them were run. The rules were not changed afterwards.
- **Post hoc (P1–P6):** written on Day 7 when modules 1–5 results were already known. They document the checks but are not evidence in the statistical sense.

Honest caveat: the build plan asked for pre-registration at the start of the project; the H-hypotheses were registered on the last day, so only the Day 7 experiments are covered.

## Pre-registered

### H1: Granularity adjustment matters above a name HHI of 0.003 — ✅ supported

In the one-factor model (the ASRF model with finitely many names), the simulated unexpected loss exceeds the analytic ASRF unexpected loss by more than 5% for every test portfolio with a name HHI of at least 0.003, by less than 5% for every portfolio with an HHI of at most 0.0015, and the add-on rises with HHI (rank correlation at least 0.9).

*Experiment:* Scale the exposures of the 25 large names by f in {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5}, keep the granular book fixed, simulate 1M one-factor scenarios per portfolio (same seed), add-on = UL_sim / UL_ASRF - 1.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `mlops/hypotheses_experiments.json:granularity.min_addon_hhi_ge_0_003` | 0.0852 > 0.0500 | holds |
| `mlops/hypotheses_experiments.json:granularity.max_addon_hhi_le_0_0015` | 0.0222 < 0.0500 | holds |
| `mlops/hypotheses_experiments.json:granularity.spearman_hhi_addon` | 1.0000 ≥ 0.9000 | holds |

### H2: Bayesian shrinkage beats the naive PD on low-default segments — ✅ supported

On fresh simulated default histories (not the one used in module 2), the posterior-mean PD has a smaller mean absolute error against the true PD than the naive default rate on segments with 0-3 training defaults in at least 80% of replications, and the median error ratio (Bayes / naive) is below 0.75.

*Experiment:* 20 fresh histories (seeds 70000-70019), training years 2014-2022, same model and prior as module 2 (1 chain, 300 warm-up, 300 draws).

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `mlops/hypotheses_experiments.json:shrinkage.bayes_better_share` | 0.9000 ≥ 0.8000 | holds |
| `mlops/hypotheses_experiments.json:shrinkage.median_mae_ratio` | 0.4789 < 0.7500 | holds |

### H3: The drift monitor flags a sector shock and stays quiet without one — ❌ not supported

With Evidently's dataset-drift rule (share of drifted columns >= 0.3), the strong real-estate shock is flagged in at least 90% of monitoring batches, unshocked batches are flagged in at most 10%, and the detection rate does not fall as the shock gets stronger.

*Experiment:* 20 seeded batches of 2,000 loans per severity (none, mild, medium, strong) drawn from the loan book; reference = a separate 5,000-loan sample. See config/mlops.yaml.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `mlops/drift.json:detection_rate.strong` | 0.1500 ≥ 0.9000 | fails |
| `mlops/drift.json:detection_rate.none` | 0.0000 ≤ 0.1000 | holds |
| `mlops/drift.json:detection_monotone` | True = True | holds |

### H4: The steering agent generalises to questions it was not tuned on — ❌ not supported

On 20 held-out questions written on day 7 with new phrasings (data/eval/heldout.jsonl), with no change to prompt, tools or verifier after seeing the results, at least 80% of answerable and multi-step questions are answered correctly and at least 90% of out-of-scope and adversarial questions are handled safely.

*Experiment:* `task agent:heldout`, scored with the same deterministic scorer as the main eval.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `agent/heldout_summary.json:answer_correct_rate` | 0.7143 ≥ 0.8000 | fails |
| `agent/heldout_summary.json:safe_rate` | 1.0000 ≥ 0.9000 | holds |

## Post hoc

### P1: Bayesian posterior mean beats naive and pooled PDs on the module-2 history — ✅ supported

Mean absolute error (bp) on low-default segments is lowest for the posterior mean.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bayes/summary.json:comparison.bayes_mean.mean_abs_error_bp_low_default` | 7.0726 < 15.1277 | holds |
| `bayes/summary.json:comparison.bayes_mean.mean_abs_error_bp_low_default` | 7.0726 < 13.7466 | holds |

### P2: Sector diversification puts the multi-factor UL below the ASRF UL — ✅ supported

The multi-factor simulated UL is below the one-factor ASRF UL.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `credit/summary.json:sim_ul_over_asrf_ul` | 0.7708 < 1.0000 | holds |

### P3: Tail dependence (t copula) at least doubles ES — ✅ supported

ES under a t copula with 6 degrees of freedom is at least twice the Gaussian ES.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `credit/summary.json:t_copula.es_ratio_t_over_gaussian` | 3.0393 ≥ 2.0000 | holds |

### P4: Conformal intervals are close to nominal coverage — ✅ supported

Test-year coverage of the 90% CV+ intervals lies within 5 points of 90%.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bayes/summary.json:conformal.coverage` | 0.8889 ≥ 0.8500 | holds |
| `bayes/summary.json:conformal.coverage` | 0.8889 ≤ 0.9500 | holds |

### P5: Behavioural deposit modelling closes the one-year funding gap — ✅ supported

The cumulative 1-year gap is negative contractually and non-negative behaviourally.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `alm/summary.json:ladder.cum_gap_1y_contractual_eur` | −3,368,142,281.0000 < 0.0000 | holds |
| `alm/summary.json:ladder.cum_gap_1y_behavioural_eur` | 294,533,906.4000 ≥ 0.0000 | holds |

### P6: Re-allocation adds at least half a point of RAROC at unchanged capital — ✅ supported

Re-simulated RAROC after optimisation exceeds today's RAROC by at least 0.5 points.

| Quantity | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `steering/summary.json:optimiser.raroc_after_resimulated − steering/summary.json:optimiser.raroc_before` | 0.0103 ≥ 0.0050 | holds |

## H2 data: shrinkage on fresh histories

20 replications: Bayes better in 90%, median MAE ratio 0.48, mean MAE 8.2 bp (Bayes) vs 14.0 bp (naive). Per replication: `results/mlops/shrinkage.csv`.
